findings.description: A session card now says 'question — see Needs you' instead of printing the question. That is a problem for an unminted session. Its card is labelled '(unminted session id)' but its Needs you line is labelled '(session id outside the minted shape; inspect the store)' and has no view link. With two unminted sessions that both have a question, the operator cannot tell which card goes with which line. Consider keeping the question text on cards for sessions that are not minted.

The renderOverview JSDoc says the page lists 'the open PRs not already in Needs you', but pullRequestsSection now prints only a count, since every open PR has its own Needs you line. A reader would look for a separate PR list that does not exist. Reword it to 'the open PRs' count'.

prFacts(pr, view) is a new three-line helper with one caller, the `pr === undefined ? '' : prFacts(pr, view)` branch in needsSection (general.md §Altitude / YAGNI). Inlining it at that call site removes the function and its `view` parameter.

process_issues.description: The consolidator was not spawned: only three minor findings came back, each a different root cause, so I deduplicated inline. Context and maintainability were skipped: no spec, protocol or infra surface was touched, and maintainability is off the default roster. Spec was skipped because no spec source or closing issue was found. Correctness ran as two instances because the diff exceeds 400 lines: one on the overview service and utils, one on the dashboard service and tests. I dropped one simplicity nit because its reviewer rated it low confidence and had not verified it (a MachineLoad alias that might duplicate an exported type). I also dropped the security reviewer's out-of-scope note that a merged session can have a fix-committed or question line: last round's validation already refuted that, since openPr is set only for merged sessions and fixCommitted only for awaiting-review ones.

The conventions reviewer did not open web-dashboard.test.ts and did not read testing.md, so the test file was not checked against the testing conventions. Its first git diff also failed with a sandbox error on .git/config.worktree.lock; a retry with narrower paths worked.
